questions.q: The World Wide Web Consortium (W3C) was founded in 1994 by:
questions.e: The W3C was founded in 1994 by Tim Berners-Lee, who is credited with inventing the World Wide Web.

questions.q: Web Engineering is best defined as:
o: the use of systematic and quantifiable approaches for the specification, implementation, operation and maintenance of high-quality Web applications
a way to design static HTML pages only
questions.e: Web Engineering comprises the use of systematic and quantifiable approaches to accomplish the specification, implementation, operation and maintenance of high-quality Web applications, and the scientific study of these approaches.

questions.q: Web Engineering is regarded as:
o: an independent branch of software engineering
questions.e: Web Engineering is an independent branch of software engineering; its basic principles can be described similarly to those of software engineering.

questions.q: A Web application is defined as:
o: a desktop program with no network access
a software system based on W3C technologies and standards that provides web-specific resources such as content and services through a Web browser
any file stored on a hard disk
questions.e: A Web application is a software system based on the technologies and standards of the W3C that provides web-specific resources such as content and services through a user interface, the Web browser.

questions.q: A Web server is a computer system that:
o: displays web pages to the user
questions.e: A Web server is a computer system that processes requests via HTTP; the Web browser is the software used to access the web.

questions.q: Which of the following is a basic principle of Web Engineering?
o: avoiding any planning to save time
systematic development of a Web application in phases with continuous audit of the process
questions.e: Basic principles of Web Engineering include clearly defined goals and requirements, systematic development in phases, careful planning of these phases, and continuous audit of the entire development process.

questions.q: Document-centric Web sites are characterized by:
o: dynamically generated pages from a database
static HTML documents that require manual changes to update information
questions.e: Document-centric Web sites are static HTML documents on a Web server; manual changes are required to update information. They are simple and stable but incur high management costs and risk inconsistent/outdated content.

questions.q: Interactive Web applications first emerged with the introduction of:
o: the Common Gateway Interface (CGI) and HTML forms
questions.e: With the introduction of the Common Gateway Interface (CGI) and HTML forms, interactive Web applications emerged, offering a first simple form of interactivity via forms, radio buttons and selection menus.

questions.q: Online banking, online shopping and booking systems are examples of which category of Web application?
questions.e: Transactional Web applications let users perform updates on the underlying content (not just read), requiring database systems; examples include online banking, online shopping and booking systems.

questions.q: A single point of access to multiple services in a particular domain (e.g. Google, Yahoo) characterizes which category?
questions.e: Portal-oriented Web applications provide a single point of access to multiple services in one or multiple domains; examples include Google and Yahoo, plus specialized business, health-sector and community portals.

questions.q: Collaborative Web applications (e.g. e-Learning systems, chat rooms) are especially used for:
questions.e: Whereas workflow-based applications require structured processes, collaborative Web applications are used for cooperation in unstructured operations (groupware); examples include e-Learning systems, scheduling systems and chat rooms.

questions.q: Providing customized services anytime, anywhere and for any device describes which category of Web application?
questions.e: Ubiquitous Web applications provide customized services anytime, anywhere and for any device, taking into account device limitations and usage context (e.g. showing a restaurant's daily menu on the phones of nearby users).

questions.q: The primary goal of the Semantic Web is to:
o: make information machine-readable, not merely human-readable
eliminate the need for web servers
questions.e: The Semantic Web aims to present information not merely for humans but also in a machine-readable form, facilitating knowledge management, linking, reuse and recommender systems.

questions.q: A Rich Internet Application (RIA) is characterized by:
o: running in a Web browser without installation while offering desktop-like features and asynchronous interaction
questions.e: Rich Internet Applications run in a Web browser and require no software installation, yet retain the features and functionality of traditional desktop applications, representing the evolution from static request-response to a dynamic, asynchronous interface.

questions.q: Regarding the technical infrastructure of Web applications, a key point about 'inhomogeneity' is that:
o: only the browser can be configured
both server and browser are fully controlled by the developer
neither server nor browser can be configured
the Web server can be configured as desired, but users' browsers and preferences cannot be influenced
questions.e: Inhomogeneity: development depends on server and browser; the Web server can usually be configured and operated as desired, but there is no way to influence users' browsers, their versions and preferences.

questions.q: Which of the following is a commonly cited reason why Web projects fail?
o: poor usability, poor performance, and security breaches
questions.e: Reasons Web projects fail include not meeting functionality/user needs, poor usability, poor performance, security breaches, poor maintainability/scalability, immature technology, schedule/cost over-runs, and poor project management.

questions.q: Instagram and weblogs (blogs) are examples of which category of Web application?
questions.e: The Social Web provides socializing facilities to a targeted audience where people with similar interests interact and provide their identity to a community; examples include Instagram and weblogs (blogs).

questions.q: Workflow-based Web applications are driven largely by the availability of Web services in order to guarantee:
questions.e: Workflow-based Web applications handle workflows within or between companies, and a driving force is the availability of Web services to guarantee interoperability; examples include Business-to-Business solutions and e-commerce.

questions.q: A scripting language is a specialized programming language designed to:
o: compile directly to machine code ahead of time
automate tasks within a particular software environment
define the structure of a database
questions.e: A scripting language is a specialized programming language designed to automate tasks within a particular software environment; JavaScript is such a language used to enhance web pages.

questions.q: JavaScript was initially created to 'make webpages alive' and was originally called:
questions.e: JavaScript was initially created to make webpages alive and was originally called 'LiveScript'.

questions.q: Standards for JavaScript are produced by:
questions.e: ECMA produces the standards for JavaScript (the ECMAScript standard).

questions.q: In a JavaScript implementation, the scripting engine acts like:
o: an interpreter that turns script into machine code on the fly at execution time
a compiler that produces a standalone executable
questions.e: A JavaScript implementation has two components: a scripting engine (like an interpreter that turns script into machine code on the fly at execution time) and a hosting environment (which provides environment-specific capabilities).

questions.q: Objects that are provided by the scripting engine are known as native objects, whereas objects provided by the hosting environment are known as:
questions.e: Native objects are provided by the scripting engine; host objects are provided by the hosting environment. Both supply capabilities to JavaScript programs through objects.

questions.q: Of the three languages web developers must learn, the roles are: HTML for content, CSS for layout, and JavaScript for:
o: programming the behavior of web pages
questions.e: HTML defines the content of web pages, CSS specifies the layout, and JavaScript programs the behavior of web pages.

questions.q: JavaScript declares variables using which keyword?
questions.e: JavaScript uses the var keyword to declare variables, and an equal sign to assign values (e.g. var x = 10;).

questions.q: If the user clicks the Cancel button in a prompt dialog, the value submitted to the script is:
questions.e: If the user clicks Cancel in a prompt dialog, no string is sent; instead the prompt returns null, a JavaScript keyword signifying that a variable has no value (absence of value).

questions.q: In JavaScript, the keyword 'null' indicates:
questions.e: Null indicates the absence of value; writing a null value to the document, however, displays the word 'null' in the web page.

questions.q: Which is a valid rule for naming a JavaScript variable (identifier)?
o: it may begin with a letter, an underscore (_), or a dollar sign ($)
it must begin with a digit
questions.e: A JavaScript variable name must start with a letter, an underscore (_), or a dollar sign ($); after the first character digits may be used; no spaces or punctuation are allowed; and names are case sensitive.

questions.q: In JavaScript, all numbers are represented internally using:
o: the 64-bit floating-point format defined by IEEE 754
questions.e: JavaScript makes no distinction between integers and floating-point values; all numbers are represented as 64-bit floating-point values per the IEEE 754 standard.

questions.q: JavaScript is described as a dynamically typed language, which means:
o: you must always declare a variable's type explicitly
you do not need to specify the type of a variable, since it is determined dynamically by the engine
questions.e: JavaScript is a dynamic type language: you do not need to specify a variable's type because it is used dynamically by the engine; a var can hold numbers, strings, etc.

questions.q: In JavaScript arithmetic, the expression (true*10 + false*7) evaluates to:
questions.e: Boolean values are automatically converted (true→1, false→0), so (true*10 + false*7) becomes (1*10 + 0*7) = 10.

questions.q: The method Math.random() returns a random number in which range?
questions.e: Math.random() returns a random number between 0 (inclusive) and 1 (exclusive); it can be scaled and shifted (e.g. Math.floor(Math.random()*6)+1 for 1–6).

questions.q: The value of Math.floor(6.75) is:
questions.e: Math.floor determines the closest integer not greater than its argument, so Math.floor(6.75) is 6 (and Math.floor(1.75) is 1).

questions.q: An event handler is:
o: the function that is called when a particular event occurs
questions.e: HTML events are things that happen to elements; the function that is called when an event occurs is known as an event handler. When a GUI event occurs, the browser calls the specified event-handling function.

questions.q: When registering an event handler with addEventListener, the method takes three arguments: the event name, the handler function, and a last argument that is typically:
questions.e: addEventListener takes the event name, the function to handle it, and a last argument that is typically false.

questions.q: The document object's getElementById method, given an element's id, returns:
o: a JavaScript object representing the matching element, allowing the script to interact with it
questions.e: getElementById finds the element with the matching id attribute and returns a JavaScript object representing that element, letting the script programmatically interact with the corresponding element on the page.

questions.q: Responsive Web Design suggests that design and development should respond to the user's behavior and environment based on:
questions.e: RWD is the approach whereby design and development respond to the user's behavior and environment based on screen size, platform and orientation, using only HTML and CSS.

questions.q: Responsive Web Design uses only which technologies?
questions.e: Responsive web design uses only HTML and CSS; a responsive website serves the same page to every visitor while the layout adapts to the visitor's screen size.

questions.q: The term 'Responsive Web Design' was first coined in May 2010 by:
questions.e: The term Responsive Web Design was first coined by Ethan Marcotte in a May 2010 article in A List Apart, defining the technique via fluid grids, flexible images and media queries.

questions.q: The three fundamental techniques of Responsive Web Design are:
o: fluid (flexible) grids, flexible media/images, and media queries
questions.e: RWD is built on flexible grid-based layouts (percentage widths), flexible media/images, and media queries (from the CSS3 specification).

questions.q: The main difference between Adaptive (AWD) and Responsive (RWD) design is that:
o: AWD depends on predefined screen sizes while RWD depends on flexible, fluid grids
RWD uses fixed pixel layouts and AWD uses percentages
questions.e: AWD depends on predefined screen sizing (a layered, scripting approach), while RWD depends on flexible and fluid grids with CSS; AWD suits limited budgets/device sets, RWD suits a wide variance of devices.

questions.q: In responsive design, the viewport is:
o: the user's visible area of a web page
questions.e: The viewport is the user's visible area of a web page; it varies by device (smaller on a phone than a computer). A meta viewport tag instructs the browser how to control the page's dimensions and scaling.

questions.q: The recommended meta viewport tag for responsive pages is:
questions.e: The recommended syntax is <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">: width=device-width sets the page width to the device's screen width, and initial-scale=1 sets the initial zoom level.

questions.q: A media query is a CSS technique introduced in CSS3 that:
o: applies a block of CSS only if a certain condition (e.g. screen width) is true
questions.e: A media query (the @media rule) is a CSS3 technique that includes a block of CSS properties only if a certain condition is true, allowing different styling depending on the device.

questions.q: In Responsive Web Design, a breakpoint is:
o: a browser width at which a media query changes the layout
a fixed pixel width for all devices
a place where the server stops
questions.e: A breakpoint is a browser width that has a media query declaration to change the layout once the browser is within the declared range; from a coding perspective a breakpoint is a media query.

questions.q: In a responsive 12-column grid, the width of a single column is approximately:
questions.e: A responsive grid-view often has 12 columns totaling 100%; the percentage of one column is 100% / 12 = 8.33%.

questions.q: The 'magic formula' for computing an element's proportion in a fluid, responsive layout is:
questions.e: The proportion of a page element is the target element divided by the context, times 100: (target/context)*100. For example, 300px / 960px = 31.25%.

questions.q: To make padding and border be included in an element's total width and height (important for responsive grids), you set the CSS property:
questions.e: Setting box-sizing: border-box ensures that padding and border are included in the total width and height of the elements, which is essential when building a responsive grid-view.

questions.q: The 'Mobile First' principle means:
o: designing for desktop first and then shrinking
designing for mobile before designing for desktop or any other device
questions.e: Mobile First means designing for mobile before designing for desktop; in practice you change the design when the width gets larger than a breakpoint (e.g. 768px) rather than when it gets smaller.

questions.q: To make an image responsive so it scales down but never scales up beyond its original size, you should use:
questions.e: Setting max-width: 100% is preferred: the image scales down if it has to but never scales up larger than its original size. Setting width: 100% would allow it to scale up beyond its original size.

questions.q: When the CSS background-size property is set to 'cover':
o: the image is stretched to exactly fill, ignoring aspect ratio
the image scales to cover the entire content area, keeping aspect ratio, though some of it may be clipped
the image scales to fit and always shows fully
questions.e: With background-size: cover, the background image scales to cover the whole content area while keeping its aspect ratio, so some part may be clipped. With 'contain' it fits fully keeping aspect ratio; with '100% 100%' it stretches to fill.

questions.q: Adaptive Web Design (AWD) is particularly recommended for:
o: users with unlimited budgets and many device types
end users with a limited budget or limited device types, and for image-heavy applications
questions.e: AWD is recommended for end users with a limited budget or limited device types/screen sizes, and is better for applications with many images that do not scale well.

questions.q: A key advantage of Responsive Web Design is that:
o: it requires a separate mobile site
it needs different content per device
a single HTML document and a single CSS file are maintained, and the same SEO strategy can be kept
questions.e: Advantages of RWD include one single HTML document and one single CSS file to maintain, accessibility on any device, very little maintenance versus a separate mobile site, and keeping the same SEO strategy.

questions.q: Web application architecture is best described as:
o: the blueprint for how components such as databases, applications and middleware interact and communicate
the visual color scheme of a website
questions.e: Web application architecture is the blueprint for how different components (databases, applications, middleware) interact and communicate, specifying the protocol for exchanging data and ensuring performance, scalability and maintainability.

questions.q: Communication between the components of a generic Web architecture is generally based on:
questions.e: Communication is generally based on the request–response principle: one component (e.g. a browser) sends a request to another (e.g. a Web server), and the response is returned over the same channel (synchronous communication).

questions.q: The client side of a web application is typically developed in:
o: HTML, JavaScript and CSS within the user's web browser
questions.e: A client is developed in HTML, JavaScript and CSS and exists within the user's web browser, needing no specific OS/device adjustments; the server side uses PHP, Python, Java, Ruby on Rails, .NET or Node.js.

questions.q: The Common Gateway Interface (CGI) is:
o: an interface specification enabling web servers to execute an external program to process user requests
questions.e: CGI is an interface specification that enables web servers to execute an external program, typically to process user requests.

questions.q: Java servlets are:
o: Java classes/programs that run on a Java application server and respond to HTTP requests, extending the Web server's capabilities
questions.e: Java servlets are Java programs/classes that run on a Java application server, designed to respond to HTTP requests and extend the capabilities of the Web server.

questions.q: The three processes of Web applications are Application Download, Data Interchange, and:
questions.e: The three processes are Application Download (mobile code downloaded to the client), Presentation Flow (dynamic visual rendering of the UI), and Data Interchange (exchange of data between components or tiers).

questions.q: JDBC and ODBC are examples of APIs used for:
questions.e: For database-centric architectures, APIs such as JDBC (Java Database Connectivity) and ODBC (Open Database Connectivity) are available for integrating relational databases into Web applications.

questions.q: In the three-tier architecture, the layer described as the 'heart of the system' that handles client requests and provides access to the DBMS is the:
questions.e: In three-tier architecture the application layer is the heart of the system: it performs the logical operations, handles the client's requests from the presentation layer, and provides a way for clients to access the DBMS.

questions.q: In the MVC pattern, the component responsible for managing the application's data and business logic is the:
questions.e: In MVC, the Model manages the data and business logic; it responds to requests from the View and to instructions from the Controller to update itself.

questions.q: In the MVC pattern, the component that handles the user request is the:
questions.e: The Controller is the request handler: the user interacts with the View, which raises a URL request handled by the Controller; the Controller renders the appropriate View with the Model data as a response.

questions.q: In the MVC pattern, the View is:
o: the user interface that displays data using the Model and lets the user modify it
questions.e: The View is the user interface; it displays data using the Model to the user and also enables them to modify the data.

questions.q: Examples of View-generation technologies mentioned for web pages include:
questions.e: Examples of view generation technologies are JSP and ASP; these start with an outline of an HTML document and use programs to fill in the missing pieces, so each display can have different content.

questions.q: The basic idea of SOFEA (Service Oriented Front End Architecture) is to:
o: stop downloading from the server and shift that responsibility to the client (as in Single Page Applications)
overload the server with all presentation generation
questions.e: SOFEA, synonymous with Single Page Web Applications, is a SOA/cloud architectural style whose basic idea is to stop downloading from the server and send that responsibility to the client.

questions.q: According to SOFEA principles, the MVC design pattern belongs in the:
questions.e: SOFEA principles state that Application Download, Data Interchange and Presentation Flow must be decoupled, presentation flow is a client-side concern only, all communication uses services (REST/SOAP), and the MVC design pattern belongs in the client, not the server.

questions.q: A micro-frontend architecture is one in which:
o: the whole app is a single monolith
the backend is split into microservices
a frontend app is split into smaller, independent pieces that are built, tested and deployed independently, often by different teams
questions.e: A micro-frontend is an architectural style where a frontend app is decomposed into smaller, independent 'micro-apps' (like microservices in the backend), each typically built, tested and deployed independently, appearing to the end user on a single page.

questions.q: An isomorphic (universal) web application is one in which:
o: the app runs only on the server
the code is written twice in two languages
the app runs only in the browser
the same JavaScript codebase can run/render on both the client and the server
questions.e: An isomorphic (universal) web app is a JavaScript application that can run both on the client and the server; the same codebase (e.g. React) renders server-side and client-side, and the client then 'hydrates' the app to make it interactive.

questions.q: A key benefit of isomorphic architecture / server-side rendering (SSR) is:
o: better SEO and a faster initial load because fully rendered HTML is sent to the browser
that it cannot be crawled by search engines
questions.e: Server-side rendering in isomorphic apps helps search engines crawl content (SEO benefits) and gives a faster initial load, since fully rendered HTML is sent to the browser instead of waiting for client-side JS to render it.

questions.q: Which of the following is one of the four majorly used API styles mentioned for the application layer?
questions.e: The four majorly used API styles listed are RESTful API, SOAP, XML-RPC and JSON-RPC; these enable software components to communicate using specific protocols.

questions.q: A web (application) framework is:
o: a software platform for developing web applications and websites, offering pre-written components, code snippets and templates
questions.e: A web framework is a software platform for developing web applications and websites; it offers pre-written components, code snippets and whole application templates, and can be used for web services, web APIs and other resources.

questions.q: Ruby on Rails is written in which language, and follows which pattern?
questions.e: Ruby on Rails (by David Heinemeier Hansson) is written in Ruby and follows the Model-View-Controller pattern; its scaffolding feature can automatically generate models and views.

questions.q: The Rails feature that can automatically generate some of the models and views required for a website is called:
questions.e: The scaffolding feature offered by Rails can automatically generate some of the models and views required for a website.

questions.q: The Django web framework uses which programming language?
questions.e: Django is a backend web development framework written in Python, known for being fast, secure, scalable and versatile; it powers sites like Instagram, Pinterest and Quora.

questions.q: ASP.NET is developed by Microsoft and primarily uses which language?
questions.e: ASP.NET is developed by Microsoft using C#/VB; ASP.NET Core is a cross-platform, high-performance, lightweight backend framework supporting Windows, Mac and Linux.

questions.q: The Laravel framework, created by Taylor Otwell in 2011, uses which language and pattern?
questions.e: Laravel, created by Taylor Otwell in 2011, uses PHP and follows the MVC architectural pattern, offering features like dependency injection and server-side rendering.

questions.q: The Spring framework, popular for enterprise development, is written in which language?
questions.e: Spring (by Pivotal Software) is the most popular application development framework for enterprise Java, using techniques such as Aspect-Oriented Programming (AOP), Plain Old Java Object (POJO) and dependency injection (DI).

questions.q: Angular is a framework by Google that is based on which language?
questions.e: Angular is a TypeScript-based, open-source web app framework managed by Google; it supports the M-V-C architecture. The original AngularJS was renamed Angular after the TypeScript rewrite (Angular 4).

questions.q: Express is best described as:
o: a minimal, flexible backend framework for Node.js (JavaScript) that helps build APIs
questions.e: Express is an open-source backend framework for JavaScript/Node.js; it is minimal and flexible, helps develop competent APIs, and is used by companies like Uber and Accenture.

questions.q: React is a front-end JavaScript library created by Facebook for building user interfaces; it also enables mobile development through:
questions.e: React is a free, open-source front-end JavaScript library by Facebook for building UIs from components; the skills also apply to React Native, used to build native iOS and Android apps.

questions.q: A characteristic data-flow feature of React is:
questions.e: React features unidirectional data flow, reusable components, easy creation of dynamic applications, and can be used for both web and mobile apps (React Native).

questions.q: Vue.js employs which kind of data binding?
o: both one-way and two-way data binding
questions.e: Vue.js is a lightweight JavaScript library for UI components used to build dynamic UIs and SPAs; it employs both one-way and two-way data binding and is flexible with third-party solutions.

questions.q: Ember.js is based on which architectural pattern?
questions.e: Ember.js is a JavaScript framework based on the Model-View-ViewModel (MVVM) architecture pattern, used to build extensible single-page applications (a notable desktop example is Apple Music).

questions.q: Which frameworks are given as examples of push-based (action-based) architecture?
o: Spring MVC, Ruby on Rails and Django
questions.e: Push-based (action-based) frameworks include Spring MVC, Ruby on Rails, Sails.js, Django and CodeIgniter; pull-based (component-based) examples include JBoss, Tapestry, Lift, Wicket and JavaServer Faces.

questions.q: CodeIgniter, developed by EllisLab, uses which language?
questions.e: CodeIgniter, developed by EllisLab, is a PHP web application framework loosely based on MVC (Controller classes are required, but models and views are optional).

questions.q: MeteorJS is an open-source framework primarily used to:
o: create real-time web and mobile apps quickly with cross-platform code
questions.e: MeteorJS (Meteor) is an open-source JavaScript framework that quickly creates real-time web and mobile apps, supporting instant prototyping and cross-platform code for iOS, Android, desktop and browsers.

questions.q: The UML-based Web engineering method consists of three design steps performed iteratively:
questions.e: The method consists of three iterative steps: conceptual, navigational and presentational design, producing UML-diagram models as artifacts.

questions.q: The design of Web applications with this method is centered around which three main aspects?
questions.e: The design is centered around three main aspects of Web systems: the content, the navigational structure and the presentation; treating them separately during design pays off in maintenance.

questions.q: In this methodology, requirements are captured using:
questions.e: Following the Unified Process, use cases are proposed for capturing requirements; they force developers to define who the actors are and represent the functionality the application must fulfill for each actor.

questions.q: The notation used by this Web engineering method is:
o: a UML profile that defines a set of stereotypes for the Web domain
questions.e: The notation is a UML profile that defines a set of appropriate stereotypes for the Web using the UML extension mechanism, indicating the special properties of modeling elements compared with standard UML.

questions.q: In the online conference paper reviewing system example, which of the following is one of the identified actors?
o: the Chair of the program committee (PC chair)
questions.e: In the reviewing system example the actors are Users, Authors (submitting papers), members of the program committee (reviewers), and the Chair of the program committee (PC chair).

questions.q: Every Web application has at least how many human actors interacting with the system?
questions.e: All Web applications have at least one human actor which interacts with the system; the overall functionality can be represented as use cases.

questions.q: The conceptual (content) model is represented by which kind of UML diagram?
questions.e: Content modeling produces a model comprising the structural aspects of the content, typically in the form of a UML class diagram (and, for complex apps, behavioral aspects via state and interaction diagrams).

questions.q: In this method, classes of the conceptual model are later used to derive nodes of the Web structure, and associations are used to derive:
questions.e: Classes defined in the conceptual model are used during navigational design to derive the nodes of the Web structure, and associations are used to derive links.

questions.q: Content modelling deliberately does NOT consider which aspects?
questions.e: Content modeling transfers the information and functional requirements to a model but does not consider the hypertext character or the presentation requirements; those are postponed to the navigational and presentational steps.

questions.q: For complex Web applications, the behavioral aspects of content can be modelled using:
questions.e: While pure data modeling (a class diagram) suffices for static apps, complex Web applications may also require behavioral aspects of content, achieved with state and interaction diagrams.

questions.q: This Web engineering design method is based on which software development process?
questions.e: The method concentrates on the analysis and design workflows of an engineering process based on the Unified Process (Jacobson, Booch & Rumbaugh), adapted for Web applications.

questions.q: To present hypertext/navigational requirements within use cases, which UML stereotype is used?
questions.e: The «navigation» stereotype is used to present hypertext/navigational requirements in the use case model.

questions.q: Hypertext modelling is based on the concepts of:
questions.e: Hypertext modelling is based on the concepts of nodes (i.e. pages or documents) and navigation between these nodes (links); the content model forms its basis.

questions.q: The navigation space model is specified as:
o: a view on the content model that specifies which objects can be visited by navigation
questions.e: The navigation space model is specified as a view on the content model; it specifies which objects can be visited by navigation. Various navigation space models can define alternative hypertext views.

questions.q: A navigational class is represented in UML using which stereotype?
questions.e: A navigational class models a class whose instances are visited by the user during navigation; it is represented using the UML stereotype «navigational class» and given the same name as the corresponding conceptual class.

questions.q: In the navigation space model, associations are interpreted as representing:
o: direct navigability from the source navigation class to the target navigation class
questions.e: Associations in the navigation space model represent direct navigability from the source navigation class to the target; they are directed (with an arrow) and each directed end has a role name and explicit multiplicity.

questions.q: By the role-naming convention in the navigation space model, if an association end has a multiplicity greater than one, the role name defaults to:
o: the plural form of the target class name
questions.e: If no explicit role name is given: if the multiplicity is ≤ 1 the target class name is used as the role name; if the multiplicity is > 1 the plural form of the target class name is used.

questions.q: The purpose of the navigational structure model (as opposed to the navigation space model) is to define:
o: how a particular node can be reached by navigation, adding orientation aids
questions.e: The navigation space model alone does not define how a node is reached; the navigational structure model refines it to provide navigation and orientation aids (indexes, guided tours, menus, queries).

questions.q: Which of the following are the access primitives used in the navigational structure model?
o: indexes, guided tours, queries and menus
questions.e: The access primitives (additional navigational nodes to access instances of navigational classes) are indexes, guided tours, queries and menus.

questions.q: An index is modeled by:
o: a composite object containing an arbitrary number of index items, each with a name and a link to an instance of a navigational class
a fixed set of menu items
questions.e: An index is a composite object containing an arbitrary number of index items; each index item is an object with a name that owns a link to an instance of a navigational class.

questions.q: A guided tour is modeled by an object that provides:
o: sequential access to the instances of a navigational class (using the {ordered} property)
questions.e: A guided tour is modeled by an object that provides sequential access to the instances of a navigational class; the connecting directed association has the {ordered} property.

questions.q: A query, as an access primitive, is modeled by an object that has:
o: a query string as an attribute
questions.e: A query is modeled by an object which has a query string as an attribute (e.g. given by an OCL select operation); a query with several results first leads to an index for selecting a particular instance.

questions.q: A menu is modeled by a composite object that contains a fixed number of menu items, where each menu item has:
o: a constant (frozen) name and a link to a navigational class instance or an access element
questions.e: A menu is a composite object containing a fixed number of menu items; each menu item has a constant name (the {frozen} property) and owns a link either to an instance of a navigational class or to an access element.

questions.q: Which of the following is a prerequisite for constructing the navigational (space) model?
o: the conceptual model, use case model and navigational requirements
questions.e: The prerequisites for the navigational model are the conceptual model, the use case model and the navigational requirements.

questions.q: When enhancing a navigation space model with indexes, guided tours and queries, one considers only those associations that have:
o: multiplicity greater than one at the directed association end
questions.e: The enhancement rule states: consider only those associations of the navigation space model which have multiplicity greater than one at the directed association end, and for each choose one or more access elements to realize the navigation.

questions.q: The navigational structure model is systematically constructed from the navigation space model in two steps:
o: first enhance with indexes/guided tours/queries, then derive menus
questions.e: The navigational structure model is constructed in two steps: first enhance the navigation space model by indexes, guided tours and queries; then directly derive the menus that represent possible navigation choices.

questions.q: Presentation modelling deals with:
o: how information in the navigation space and access structures is presented to the user (the user interface and look and feel)
questions.e: Presentation modelling addresses how the information within the navigation space and the access structures is presented to the user; it deals with the user interface and the look and feel, producing an abstract interface design like a UI sketch.

questions.q: The presentation model focuses on:
o: the structural organization of the presentation, not the physical appearance
questions.e: The presentation model focuses on the structural organization of the presentation, not on physical appearance (special formats, colors, etc.); those decisions are left to the implementation phase, though layout may hint at relative position and size.

questions.q: Decisions about specific colors and formats are deliberately left to which phase?
questions.e: The presentation model does not fix physical appearance (colors, formats); such decisions are left to the implementation phase.

questions.q: Presentation model elements are described on three hierarchical levels:
o: presentation page, presentation unit and presentation element
questions.e: The three hierarchical levels are: a presentation page (a visualization unit), a presentation unit (a group of related UI elements / logical fragment presenting a node), and a presentation element (the basic building block).

questions.q: A presentation element is the basic building block and can include:
o: text, images, audio and similar information items
questions.e: Presentation elements are the basic building blocks representing a node's set of information; they can include text, images, audio, etc.

questions.q: A frameset, in the presentation model, is:
o: a container of presentational objects or other framesets
questions.e: A frameset is a container of presentational objects or other (sub)framesets; it is stereotyped by «frameset».

questions.q: A presentational class models:
o: the presentation of a navigational class or an access primitive (index, guided tour, query or menu)
questions.e: A presentational class models the presentation of a navigational class or an access primitive; its instances are containers comprising elements like texts, images, video/audio, anchors and collections.

questions.q: Presentation modelling produces a two-fold result: a static presentation model describing the page structure, and a dynamic presentation model describing:
o: the behavior-oriented aspects of the UI, e.g. which button activates a function
questions.e: The static presentation model gives a uniform presentation concept and page structure (headers, footers, forms), while the dynamic presentation model describes behavior-oriented aspects, e.g. which button to click to activate an application function.

questions.q: In a menu-based presentation, framesets partition the presentation so that:
o: the left frame always shows the main menu and the right frame shows the actual content
the whole page is a single frame
questions.e: In a menu-based presentation, framesets partition the presentation into frames where the left frame always shows the main menu and the right frame shows the actual content.

questions.q: A map-based presentation (also known as the tree-structured technique) shows:
o: the main menu on the left
the actual navigation tree in the left frame and the corresponding content in the right frame, reducing the 'lost in hyperspace' problem
a single window with no frames
questions.e: In a map-based presentation the left frame shows the actual navigation tree and the right frame shows the corresponding content; this tree-structured technique visualizes the navigation space and reduces the 'lost in hyperspace' syndrome.

questions.q: The dynamic aspects of the presentation are captured by a:
questions.e: The dynamic aspects of the presentation are formed by a window flow model, which describes the behavior of the presentational objects (changes on the UI when the user interacts), specifying when windows open, close and coexist.

questions.q: To represent the control flow between windows (the interaction model), the method uses:
questions.e: Control flow between windows is represented by interaction models showing which windows are open and which frameset is displayed in each window at a given moment; for this purpose UML sequence diagrams are used.

questions.q: An anchor, as a presentation element, is:
o: a clickable piece of text that is the starting point of a navigation to other nodes
questions.e: An anchor is a clickable piece of text which is the starting point of a navigation, establishing the relationship to other nodes; a button is a clickable area with an associated action.

questions.q: In the presentation model, a window includes at least two buttons, namely one to close the window and one to:
o: transform (reduce) the window into an icon
questions.e: A window is the area where framesets or presentational objects are displayed; it can be moved, resized and reduced to an icon, and includes at least two buttons: one to iconize the window and one to close it.

questions.q: Usability is defined as the extent to which a product can be used by specified users in a specified context to achieve specified goals:
questions.e: Usability is the extent to which a product can be used by specified users within a specified usage context to achieve specified goals effectively, efficiently and satisfactorily.

questions.q: In the definition of usability, achieving goals 'effectively' means:
questions.e: Effectively means completely and exactly; efficiently means at a justifiable cost relative to the achievement; and satisfactorily refers to user satisfaction.

questions.q: During design for usability, one must consider the product's goals, the usage context, and:
questions.e: For usability one must consider, in each individual case, the goals, the users (who they are), and the use context, and control development with appropriate feedback mechanisms.

questions.q: User-based usability evaluation methods:
o: involve end-users in evaluation and optimization during design/prototyping/implementation and are accurate but expensive and time-consuming
questions.e: User-based methods involve end-users in the evaluation and optimization of usability during design, prototyping and implementation; they are accurate but expensive and time consuming. Expert methods instead rely on experts' experience and theoretical models.

questions.q: As a rule of thumb for color use in Web design, the upper limit is roughly:
questions.e: Colors should not be used excessively; as a rule of thumb, roughly five colors represent the upper limit, and extreme/highly saturated hues should be avoided. Color should not be the sole criterion to highlight areas.

questions.q: Which is a recommended text-layout guideline for Web pages?
o: avoid block letters/small caps and avoid patterned backgrounds, keeping text concise in short paragraphs
use lots of block letters and small caps
questions.e: Reading on screen is less efficient than on paper, so block letters and small caps should be avoided, backgrounds should not have patterns, and text should be concise and laid out in short paragraphs in the user's language.

questions.q: A recommended page-structure guideline is to:
o: avoid the need for horizontal scrolling and keep important interaction elements (like menus) always visible
questions.e: Page structure guidelines: avoid the need for horizontal scrolling; ensure important interaction elements such as menus never become invisible due to scrolling; use column-oriented layout; do not overload pages; and allow pages to be printed.

questions.q: A well-designed navigation structure must above all avoid:
o: giving feedback on the current position
the 'getting lost in hyperspace' syndrome caused by non-linear navigation
questions.e: The 'getting lost in hyperspace' syndrome due to non-linear navigation has to be avoided; a clear structure provides a sitemap, constant feedback on the current position ('Where am I?'), and clear information about content and reachable items.

questions.q: The date '11/03/2003' is used as an example of a multiculturality problem because it means:
o: March 11 in Europe but November 3 in the USA (ambiguous date format)
questions.e: Date formats differ by culture: 11/03/2003 would be March 11 in Europe but November 3 in the USA; a correction to 11/Mar/2003 prevents the ambiguity. Colors, symbols and language also carry cultural differences.

questions.q: Which is an example of a confidence-generating measure for a commercial Web application?
o: presenting an 'About Us' page and real-world contact information (postal address, phone, e-mail)
questions.e: Confidence-generating measures include an 'About Us' page, real-world contact information (address, e-mail, ideally toll-free phone), FAQ/chat/message boards, data-privacy activities, and customer-friendly warranty or money-back policies.

questions.q: In a usability engineering process, the role responsible for checking and evaluating models, guidelines and standards, conducting tests and issuing change requests is the:
questions.e: The usability expert checks and evaluates models, guidelines and standards, conducts tests, analyzes results and issues change requests. The systems analyst handles requirements analysis and conceptual design; the interface designer designs the look and feel; the implementer builds the system.

questions.q: Which usability-engineering role is in charge of requirements analysis and conceptual design?
questions.e: The systems analyst is in charge of the requirements analysis and the conceptual design; other roles are the interface designer, usability expert and implementer.

questions.q: In usability engineering, 'anonymous' Web applications refer to:
o: intranet software with known user groups
information-centered Web applications (with unknown, general users)
questions.e: Anonymous Web applications include information-centered Web applications (general, unknown users), whereas non-anonymous Web applications correspond to conventional software on a Web platform (normally an intranet) with known user target groups.

questions.q: A typical outcome of the requirements-analysis phase of the usability engineering process is:
o: user profiles, task analysis/use case model, platform specifications and usability goals
questions.e: The requirements-analysis phase produces user profiles (especially for non-anonymous apps), task analysis/scenarios/use case model, platform property specifications, and qualitative/quantitative usability goals.

questions.q: Achieving usability for the final product is characterized as:
o: an ongoing series of actions (hence called usability engineering)
a one-time task done at the end
questions.e: Knowing product characteristics beforehand helps, but achieving usability for the final product is an ongoing series of actions — hence the term usability engineering.

questions.q: According to Myers (1979), testing is best described as:
o: running a program with the intent to find errors
running a program to prove it has no errors
questions.e: If we run a program with the intent to find errors, then we talk about testing (Myers 1979). Testing evaluates the quality of a product and improves it by identifying defects and problems.

questions.q: In testing, an error is present when:
o: the actual result from a test run does not comply with the expected result
the program uses too much memory
questions.e: An error is present if the actual result from a test run does not comply with the expected result; each deviation from the value typically expected by users is also considered an error.

questions.q: The expected result of a test is typically specified in the:
questions.e: The expected result is specified, for example, in the requirements definition; for Web applications this is complicated because requirements are defined over a period of time.

questions.q: A single test case (per IEEE 610.12-1990) describes:
o: a set of inputs, execution conditions and expected results used to test a specific aspect of the object under test
questions.e: A single test case describes a set of inputs, execution conditions and expected results, which are used to test a specific aspect of the object under test (IEEE standard 610.12-1990).

questions.q: The main objective of testing is to:
o: find errors rather than show their absence
questions.e: The main objective of testing is to find errors rather than showing their absence; a test run is successful if errors are detected, giving insight into the problems.

questions.q: Which set correctly lists the six principal quality characteristic categories to be tested?
o: planning, preparing, performing, reporting, auditing, closing
functionality, reliability, usability, efficiency, maintainability, portability
speed, cost, color, layout, security, size
input, process, output, storage, control, feedback
questions.e: The six principal categories of characteristics are functionality, reliability, usability, efficiency, maintainability and portability.

questions.q: Unit tests are:
o: tests of the complete integrated system
tests done only by the client
tests of the smallest testable units (classes, Web pages), done by the developer during implementation
questions.e: Unit tests test the smallest testable units (classes, Web pages, etc.) independently; unit testing is done by the developer during implementation.

questions.q: Integration tests are used to:
o: evaluate the interaction between distinct, separately tested units once integrated
test the whole system with the client
test the smallest units in isolation
questions.e: Integration tests evaluate the interaction between distinct and separately tested units once they have been integrated; they are performed by a tester, a developer, or both jointly.

questions.q: System tests are typically performed by:
o: a specialized test team, on the complete integrated system
questions.e: System tests test the complete, integrated system and are typically performed by a specialized test team.

questions.q: Acceptance tests are characterized by:
o: being evaluated in cooperation with the client using real conditions and real data
being done by the developer with dummy data
questions.e: Acceptance tests evaluate the system in cooperation with or under the auspices of the client, in an environment close to production, using real conditions and real data.

questions.q: Beta tests are:
o: informal tests (without test plans/cases) letting friendly users work with early versions to give feedback
tests performed only by the client's lawyers
formal tests with detailed test plans and cases
questions.e: Beta tests let friendly users work with early versions of a product for early feedback; they are informal tests without test plans and test cases, relying on the number and creativity of potential users.

questions.q: 'Broken links' (links pointing to non-existing pages) are a frequent error associated with which testing challenge?
questions.e: For the hypertext structure, one must ensure pages are reachable and that no links are broken; broken links are frequent errors when statically pre-defined links become invalid.

questions.q: The four steps of the conventional test approach are:
questions.e: The conventional test approach has four steps: Planning (quality goals, strategy, plans, metrics, environment), Preparing (techniques, tools, test cases/data), Performing (run and evaluate), and Reporting (summarize results and produce reports).

questions.q: Compared with conventional approaches, agile approaches to testing focus on:
o: collaboration, treating testing as an integrated development activity
questions.e: Agile approaches focus on collaboration whereas conventional approaches focus on planning and project management; in agile, testing is an integrated development activity.

questions.q: In Extreme Programming, 'test-first development' means:
o: writing tests before the code, so the developer pair thinks about the 'what' before the 'how'
writing tests only after the code is complete
questions.e: Test-first development writes tests before the code, ensuring the developer pair thinks about the 'what' before implementing the 'how'; automated tests can then help with integration.

questions.q: In XP practices influencing testing, a benefit of pair programming is that it:
o: removes the need for a customer
accelerates knowledge exchange between roles and helps detect errors early
questions.e: Pair programming accelerates the exchange of knowledge between various roles and within the team, and helps detect errors early; an on-site customer clarifies requirements and co-develops functional tests.

questions.q: The test scheme is described by three dimensions: test objects, quality characteristics, and:
o: the phase/time of the software lifecycle at which the combination is tested
questions.e: Test objects and quality characteristics form two dimensions; the third dimension specifies at what phase or time of the software lifecycle the combination of the two needs to be tested.
